modules.title: Orientation: the SBR exam and how it is assessed

claims.text: The syllabus is assessed by a three-hour fifteen-minute examination.

citations.quote: The syllabus is assessed by a three-hour fifteen-minute examination.

claims.text: Section A will consist of two scenario-based questions. The first question will be worth 30 marks and the second question will be worth 20 marks.

citations.quote: Section A will consist of two scenario-based questions. The first question will be worth 30 marks and the second question will be worth 20 marks.

claims.text: Candidates will need to discuss issues in group accounting and use a spreadsheet to adjust a consolidated financial statement.

citations.quote: Candidates will need to discuss issues in group accounting and use a spreadsheet to adjust a consolidated financial statement.

claims.text: The second question in Section A will require candidates to consider the reporting implications and the ethical implications of specific events in a contemporary scenario.

citations.quote: The second question in Section A will require candidates to consider the reporting implications and the ethical implications of specific events in a contemporary scenario.

claims.text: Students will be required to answer a further two questions, each worth 25 marks.

lessons.title: What can be examined, and when

claims.text: For most examinations (not tax), regulations issued or legislation passed on or before 31 August annually will be examinable from 1 September of the following year to 31 August of the year after that.

citations.quote: For most examinations (not tax), regulations issued or legislation passed on or before 31 August annually, will be examinable from 1 September of the following year to 31 August of the year after that.

claims.text: Regulations issued or legislation passed in accordance with the above dates will not be examinable if the effective date is in the future, unless explicitly stated otherwise in this syllabus and study guide or examinable documents.

citations.quote: Regulations issued or legislation passed in accordance with the above dates will not be examinable if the effective date is in the future, unless explicitly stated otherwise in this syllabus and study guide or examinable documents.

claims.text: The term issued or passed relates to when regulation or legislation has been formally approved. The term effective relates to when regulation or legislation must be applied to an entity’s transactions and business practices.

citations.quote: The term issued or passed relates to when regulation or legislation has been formally approved. The term effective relates to when regulation or legislation must be applied to an entity’s transactions and business practices.

claims.text: The passage does not say which date the phrase "in the future" is measured from, so the ACCA examinable documents must be consulted to settle borderline cases.

citations.quote: will not be examinable if the effective date is in the future, unless explicitly stated otherwise in this syllabus and study guide or examinable documents

claims.basis: The quoted rule refers to the future without naming a reference date, and it points to the examinable documents for exceptions.

lessons.title: Stepping up from FR: what changes at SBR
lessons.sourceNote: Based on an ACCA article dated June 2025; the 2026-27 syllabus controls where they differ.

claims.text: The article says candidates will score very little in this exam for simply regurgitating the requirements of IFRS Accounting Standards.

citations.quote: You will score very little in this exam for simply regurgitating the requirements of IFRS Accounting Standards.

claims.text: The article says that in SBR analysis and interpretation has a very different meaning from FR and is tested in much more depth.

citations.quote: was in FR; however in SBR it has a very different meaning. AT THIS LEVEL, ‘ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION’ IS TESTED IN MUCH MORE DEPTH.

claims.text: The article says a common misconception is that a reporting exam is largely numerical, however the emphasis in SBR is on written questions.

citations.quote: A common misconception is that a reporting exam is largely numerical, however the emphasis in SBR is on written questions.

claims.text: The article says that additional performance measures are not examined in the earlier levels of the Qualification.

citations.quote: One area on the SBR syllabus that is worthy of specific mention is ‘additional performance measures’. This area is not examined in the earlier levels of the Qualification.

claims.text: The article says it is extremely important to be aware that the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards are examinable documents.

steps: Explain the accounting and financial statement consequences

worked.requirement: Explain how Section B differs from Section A in the SBR exam. (Subject matter is exam structure, so every fact below is source-verified.)
worked.weak: Section B is harder and has more writing.
worked.adequate: Section A has two scenario-based questions worth 30 and 20 marks. Section B has two questions worth 25 marks each.
worked.strong: Issue: the difference in structure and focus. Principle (syllabus): Section A is two scenario-based questions worth 30 and 20 marks; Section B is two discursive questions worth 25 marks each. Application: the first Section A question centres on group accounting and a spreadsheet task, while Section B can cover any syllabus area. Consequence: revision must cover all areas because all questions are compulsory, and Section B always needs a stakeholder viewpoint. Conclusion: plan revision across the whole syllabus and practise stakeholder-focused answers.
worked.commentary: Weak: vague and unsupported. Adequate: accurate but only restates facts. Strong: states the issue, applies the facts to the learner’s situation and draws a conclusion. The marks logic here is illustrative, not an ACCA marking scheme.
